title: Histomorphometrical Analyses of the Mouse Suprachiasmatic Nucleus
author: Sophia A.M.B. Villanueva
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and reagents Reagents 1. Cholera toxin subunit B (Recombinant), Alexa Fluor TM 555 conjugate (Invitrogen TM , catalog number: C34776 )

steps.title: Gather reagents and materials
steps.instruction: Obtain cholera toxin subunit B (recombinant), Alexa Fluor™ 555 conjugate (Invitrogen, catalog number C34776) and ensure access to Zeiss Zen software, a Zeiss AxioImager M2 (or comparable) microscope with motorized stage and AxioCam MRm for fluorescence, a Zeiss Axioskop with color Axiocam for Nissl, and Fiji/ImageJ installed.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence and Nissl images of middle SCN
steps.instruction: Using Zen Zeiss software and the appropriate microscope, acquire 2‑D images of every coronal section (20 µm for Nissl, 50 µm for DAPI/fluorescence) that contains the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) from rostral to caudal. Activate the Cy3 channel for the Alexa 555‑conjugated cholera toxin and the DAPI channel. Identify the SCN by its ventral location, shape and cell‑density using a 10× objective so that both left and right nuclei appear in one field. For each experimental “set” (one animal per group; aim for ≥5 sets, n = 5), determine the exposure time for each channel on a representative section, then keep that exposure constant for all sections of that set. Typical exposure times: Set 1 = 400 ms, Set 2 = 500 ms, Set 3 = 300 ms for the cholera toxin; DAPI 70–100 ms; Nissl 8–10 ms. Gain = 1, bit depth = 12 for all channels. Capture left and right SCN images, save each file as “<name>.czi”.

substeps.instruction: Open Zen, select Acquisition mode tab.
Activate Cy3 and DAPI channels.
Select 10× objective and locate SCN.
Set exposure for each channel on a test section; record the lowest value for the set.
Repeat exposure determination for each subsequent set.
Capture left‑right SCN images for every section.
Save files as .czi.

steps.title: Morphometrical analysis of SCN with AxioVision
steps.instruction: Convert each .czi file to .zvi (ZEN → Save As/Export). Open the .zvi in Zeiss AxioVision, apply the correct scaling (real‑world µm) by selecting the appropriate objective and clicking Activate → Apply to Image. Open the Properties window and set Display to Linear for Nissl‑stained sections or Min/Max for fluorescence. Use the Outline (or Outline spline) tool to trace the SCN border and the Length tool to draw a vertical line at the tallest part (height) and a horizontal line at the widest part (width). Keep the Properties window open to adjust annotation appearance if desired. Open the Measurement tab, click “Create table”, and export the table as <name>.csv (or copy values to Excel).

substeps.instruction: Convert .czi → .zvi.
Launch AxioVision and open .zvi.
Apply scaling: Measure menu → Scaling or Work area → Scalings → Activate appropriate objective → Apply.
Open Properties (View menu or toolbar) and set Display (Linear or Min/Max).
Select drawing tool (Outline/Outline spline) from Measure menu; trace SCN border.
Select Length tool; draw vertical line for height, horizontal line for width.
Adjust annotation style in Properties → Attributes if needed.
Open Measurement tab, click Create table, save as .csv.

steps.title: Quantify whole‑SCN fluorescence intensity (Fiji/ImageJ)
steps.instruction: Launch Fiji/ImageJ. Drag‑and‑drop each .czi file onto the Fiji window (do not use File → Open). In the Bio‑Formats Import Options, select Standard image for single‑plane or Hyperstack for Z‑stacks, enable Autoscale, set Color Options to Greyscale, check Split Channels (to separate DAPI and cholera toxin) and, for Z‑stacks, check Split Focal Planes. Click OK. Adjust brightness/contrast automatically (Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast → Auto). Open the ROI Manager (Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager). Using the freehand tool on the DAPI channel, outline the left SCN, click Add; repeat for the right SCN. Rename and save each ROI in a dedicated folder (More → Save → Rename as…). Set the scale units to microns (Specify window). Modify ROI appearance if desired. Superimpose each ROI onto the corresponding cholera toxin image, reposition with arrow keys (do not change size), and click Update. In Measure → Set Measurements, select Mean gray value and Integrated density. Measure each ROI (Analyze → Measure or ROI Manager → Measure or press M). Repeat for all sections (≥5 consecutive sections per animal). Save the Results window as a .csv file (File → Save As).

substeps.instruction: Open Fiji, drag‑and‑drop .czi files.
In Bio‑Formats Import Options set:
• Single‑plane → Standard image OR Z‑stack → Hyperstack
• Autoscale, Greyscale, Split Channels, Split Focal Planes (if Z‑stack).
Click OK to open images.
Adjust brightness/contrast: Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast → Auto.
Open ROI Manager: Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager.
Select freehand tool, outline left SCN on DAPI, Add to ROI Manager.
Repeat for right SCN, Add.
Rename ROIs, save in folder (More → Save → Rename as…).
Set scale units to microns (Specify window).
Optionally modify ROI line color/thickness (Properties).
Select ROI, switch to cholera toxin image, reposition with arrows, Update.
Set measurements: Measure → Set Measurements → check Mean gray value, Integrated density.
Measure each ROI (Analyze → Measure or ROI Manager → Measure or press M).
Repeat for all images (≥5 sections/animal).
Save results: Results window → File → Save As → .csv.

steps.title: Analyze ventral SCN fluorescence distribution (Plot Profile)
steps.instruction: Using the same left/right ROIs created above, select the Rectangle tool in Fiji. Draw a fixed‑size rectangular ROI that encloses the ventral portion of the left SCN on the cholera toxin image, then click Add in the ROI Manager and save. Move the rectangle to the ventral right SCN, Add and save (both ROIs must have identical width × height). Ensure the ROI size is recorded via ROI Manager → More → Specify. Superimpose each ROI on its respective image and click Update (do not alter size). Generate a plot profile (Analyze → Plot Profile or press K). In the Plot window, change to a vertical plot (More → Plot Defaults → Vertical). For each plot, open Data → Add Fit, select a fifth‑order polynomial (the fit used in the original study) to align intensity peaks across sections. Export the numeric data (List → then File → Save As or copy to Excel). Repeat for all sections; average the left‑side profiles and right‑side profiles separately (averaging across the 5 sections per animal) to obtain one curve per side per animal.

substeps.instruction: From previous step, keep ROI Manager open.
Select Rectangle tool.
Draw rectangle over ventral left SCN on cholera toxin image, Add to ROI Manager, save.
Move rectangle to ventral right SCN, Add, save (ensure identical dimensions).
Record ROI dimensions via ROI Manager → More → Specify.
Superimpose ROI on each image, adjust position with arrows, click Update.
Generate plot: Analyze → Plot Profile (or Command/Control K).
In Plot window, select More → Plot Defaults → Vertical.
Open Data menu → Add Fit, choose fifth‑order polynomial (or best fit).
Export plot data: List → then File → Save As (.csv) or copy to Excel.
Repeat for all sections (≥5 per animal).
Average left‑side profiles and right‑side profiles separately to obtain one curve per side per animal.
